body.statement: If \(\tau_n\to\infty\) and \(b_n\to b\in\mathbb R\), then \(\{L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\widehat\Delta^P_{\ell}-\overline\Delta\}/\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}\Rightarrow N(b,1)\), while replacing \(\widehat\Delta^P_{\ell}\) by \(\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}\) gives \(N(0,1)\). Aggregate first-order equivalence holds if and only if \(b_n\to0\), even when individual pairwise shifts do not vanish.
body.justification: The exact signed aggregate criterion preserves cross-pair cancellation that a maximum pairwise bound would erase.
body.gap: The published fifteen-pair aggregation assumes interior regularity and has no rare-link noncentrality frontier.
body.consumer: The fixed fifteen-comparison crime aggregate can be assessed without requiring every individual comparison to be safely away from link disagreement.
body.proof_tex:
Define
\[
\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{P}=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\Delta^P_\ell,
\qquad
\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{E}=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\widehat\Delta^E_\ell,
\qquad
\overline\Delta^{P}=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Delta^P_\ell.
\]
The centered characteristic-function and Taylor calculations in the pairwise proof do not use convergence, or even boundedness, of the drifting indices.  They show, jointly over the fixed \(L=15\) pairs,
\[
\frac{\widehat\Delta^P_\ell-\Delta^P_\ell}{\sqrt{\rho_n/n}}
\Rightarrow N(0,V_\ell),
\qquad
\frac{\widehat\Delta^E_\ell-\Delta_\ell}{\sqrt{\rho_n/n}}
\Rightarrow N(0,V_\ell),
\tag{1}
\]
with independent coordinates.  Positivity of the limiting coefficients and role shares implies \(V_\ell>0\), and therefore
\[
\overline V=L^{-2}\sum_{\ell=1}^LV_\ell>0.
\]
Taking the fixed linear average in (1), or equivalently substituting equal Fourier arguments in its joint characteristic function, gives
\[
\frac{\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{P}-\overline\Delta^{P}}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
\qquad
\frac{\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{E}-\overline\Delta}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{2}
\]
The second centering is the aggregate causal estimand because the identification proposition proves the pairwise population identity before averaging.

By the definition of the aggregate index, the remaining centering difference is exactly
\[
\frac{\overline\Delta^{P}-\overline\Delta}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}
=\frac{\sqrt{n/\rho_n}}{L\sqrt{\overline V}}
\sum_{\ell=1}^L(\Delta^P_\ell-\Delta_\ell)
=b_n.
\tag{3}
\]
Adding (3) to the first convergence in (2) proves the \(N(b,1)\) limit when \(b_n\to b\); the second convergence in (2) proves the exact-link \(N(0,1)\) limit.

The gradient comparison and Taylor remainder in the pairwise proof are uniform over the fixed set of pairs.  Summing them and using (3) gives
\[
\frac{\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{P}-\overline{\widehat\Delta}^{E}}
{\sqrt{\rho_n\overline V/n}}
=b_n+o_P(1).
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(b_n\to0\) implies aggregate first-order equivalence.  Conversely, if the left side of (4) converges to zero in probability, the deterministic sequence \(b_n\) must converge to zero: otherwise some subsequence has \(|b_n|\geq\varepsilon>0\), which is incompatible with (4).  This proves the if-and-only-if assertion.

To verify that aggregate equivalence need not entail pairwise equivalence, take two pairs with constant triples
\[
(c_1,c_2,c_3)=(2,2,1)
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
(c_1,c_2,c_3)=(1/2,4,1),
\]
and place every remaining pair on either exact cancellation plane.  These triples obey the coefficient box and satisfy
\[
Q_1A_1=4(\log2)^2,
\qquad Q_2A_2=-4(\log2)^2.
\]
The uniform expansion therefore cancels the two leading population shifts and leaves their sum of order \(O(\rho_nu_n^{-4})\).  To exhibit a valid subsequence, choose any \(\rho_k\downarrow0\), put \(u_k=-q(\rho_k)\), and set \(n_k=\lfloor u_k^6/\rho_k\rfloor\); define the triangular array at sample size \(n_k\) using rarity \(\rho_k\).  Then \(\sqrt{n_k\rho_k}=u_k^3\{1+o(1)\}\), so equation (3) gives \(b_{n_k}=O(u_k^{-1})\to0\), whereas each nonzero pair has \(|\Lambda_{\ell n_k}|\asymp u_k\to\infty\).  Hence cross-pair signed cancellation can produce aggregate first-order equivalence while both contributing pairwise shifts fail to vanish.
